Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:33: After all this, the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on His creatures, as it is said (Isaiah 57:16), "for I will not contend forever, nor will I be always wrathful, for the spirit would fail before Me, and the souls which I have made."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:35: And in the Midrash Ruth HaNe'elam (Zohar Chadash 79a) they explained, in brief, the seven compartments and what is punished in them; in these words:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:36: The first compartment is called Bor [Pit], and it is the uppermost compartment; and there are many angels of destruction there, like a pit that has no water but has snakes and scorpions in it - so too this compartment called Bor has many companies of angels of destruction like snakes and fiery serpents for whom there is no charm. Three appointed officers rule in Gehinnom, and they are under the hand of Dumah: Mashchit [Destroyer], Af [Anger], and Cheimah [Wrath], and all the others are appointed under them; and all those compartments run to and fro and judge there the souls of the wicked. And all those companies of angels of destruction shake all of Gehinnom, and their voice is heard in the firmament, and the voice of the wicked among them cries out and says, woe, woe, and there is no mercy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:37: He said afterward: in the first compartment they judge those who "pluck mallow from the bushes" - those who interrupt words placed on the Tablets [i.e., words of Torah] for idle chatter; and those who do not give honor to Torah scholars - though one who demeans Torah scholars is not judged in this place, but is judged in Tit HaYaven [Miry Clay]; and one who curses a deaf person and the like; and one who passes behind a synagogue at the time the congregation is praying; and one who tells his fellow's praise before someone who hates him, [thereby bringing him to] harm - all these and the like are judged in the first compartment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:38: The second compartment is called Shachat [Pit/Corruption], and it is a green fire, and there is nothing there but darkness, and there is no mercy there at all; and there they judge all those who speak ill of Torah scholars after their death, and one who shames his fellow in a matter of halachah so that others will not learn from him, and one who is arrogant not for the sake of Heaven, and one who honors himself through his fellow's disgrace, and one who knows that his fellow will stumble in a point of halachah, and they are in the same town, and does not inform him before he stumbles, and rejoices - he or others; and one who has a synagogue in his town and does not enter to pray in it; and one who is not accommodating to his fellow in a matter of halachah when they are in the same town; and one who eats from a meal that does not suffice its host; and one who raises his hand against his fellow even though he did not strike him; and one who curses his fellow in jest in a manner that brings him shame - all these are judged in this compartment, and all like them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:39: And concerning what was said, "one who knows that his fellow will stumble in a matter of halachah and does not inform him" - Rashbi said (Shelach 167a) that a certain sage did this to his fellow; and it says there, concerning the souls that would come to Rashbi, peace be upon him, to tell him of the words of the Garden of Eden and supernal secrets, that meanwhile one [soul] flew away and was hidden from them, and after a while returned to them. He said to them: I was destined to enter, and they were all in one crown, [a session] judging the case of a certain person who stands at the gate of the Garden of Eden, and those cherubim held him and did not let him enter there, and he was in distress among them, and he cried out cries at the gate, and all the righteous ones there heard, and now all the members of the academy gather to go in to the Messiah-King to examine his case. And afterward they told his punishment and said: they judged his case and the Messiah decreed that this person should remain outside, in that distress, forty days; at the end of forty days they would torment him with the torment of Gehinnom for an hour and a half. And all this because one day, one of the colleagues was expounding words of Torah, and when he reached a certain point, this person knew he would stumble on it, and he said to the colleagues, be silent, do not say anything - and because the colleagues kept silent, the colleague stumbled on that matter and was ashamed; and it was that shame which this person caused that led them to judge him with this harsh judgment, because the Holy One, blessed be He, does not wish to let the mockery of the Torah pass even to the extent of a hair's breadth - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:40: And similarly it is explained there (171b) concerning a certain child who shamed his teacher with difficult questions, and was punished; in these words: and because they wished to judge his case openly, he was saved from it - for he would shame his teacher before everyone with his questions and difficulties, and did not concern himself with going to someone else to fix his learning, and weakened his teacher's spirit; and because they did not wish to judge him with harsh judgment, therefore, even though he was saved from the Master of Judgment, he was not saved here - seven days his image was not completed here, and he would be washed with extra pain before everyone all those seven days until his image was completed - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:41: The third compartment is called Dumah, and there are judged all those haughty of spirit who exalt their hearts in halachah before the people not for the sake of Heaven, and those who speak evil-speech, and one who is arrogant in giving legal rulings, and one who judges his fellow to the side of guilt, and one who lends to his fellow with interest, and one who shows favoritism [distorts] in Torah not according to halachah, and one who does not answer "amen" to the one who recites a blessing, and one who makes an interruption [pesek] - such as one who, in the midst of his prayer, stops and speaks of another matter, and stops again - he is called a "posek"; and one who mocks his fellow or an elder who has forgotten his learning; and one who sees a matter of impropriety in his fellow and does not inform him privately, between the two of them - all these are judged there, and all like them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:42: The fourth compartment is called Tit HaYaven [Miry Clay]; there are judged the haughty of spirit, and all those who answer the poor and the oppressed with insolence, and one who sees a poor person in distress and does not lend to him until he seeks his own benefit from it, and one who withholds a hired worker's wages, and one who emits seed in vain, and one who consorts with a gentile woman or a menstruating woman, and one who takes a pledge from a poor person and does not return his pledged items to him when he has nothing else, and one who perverts justice, and one who takes a bribe - all of them are judged in this compartment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:43: The fifth compartment is called Sheol, and there are judged the informers, and the heretics, and those who deny the Torah, and those who deny the resurrection of the dead; and of these it is said (Job 7:9), "as the cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to Sheol shall not come up." And of the rest of the sinners it is written (I Samuel 2:6), "the LORD kills and makes alive; He brings down to Sheol and brings up."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:44: The sixth compartment is Tzalmavet [Shadow of Death], and there are judged all those who lay with their mothers, and with a menstruating woman.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:45: The seventh compartment is Eretz Tachtit [Nethermost Land]; whoever descends there never ascends again, as it is said (Malachi 3:21), "and you shall trample the wicked," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:46: And in the Zohar (Terumah 150b) it says that there is a place in Gehinnom called "boiling excrement," and in it are judged all those who sinned and caused the multitude to sin, and likewise those who emit seed in vain deliberately. In these words: there is a place in Gehinnom, and levels there, called "boiling excrement"; and there is the filth of the souls that were soiled with all the filth of this world and are [now] refined and ascend, and that filth remains there; and those evil levels, called thus "boiling excrement," are appointed over that remaining filth, and the fire of Gehinnom rules over that remaining filth. And there are wicked ones who are constantly soiled with their sins and are not refined of them, and die without repentance - those who sinned and caused others to sin, and were constantly stiff-necked and did not humble themselves before their Master in this world - these are judged there in that filth and in that "boiling excrement," and never leave there. Those who corrupt their ways upon the earth and did not care for the honor of their Master in this world - all these are judged there for generations upon generations and do not leave there. On Sabbaths and on New Moons and on festival seasons and on holidays, in that place the fire settles and they are not judged, but they do not leave from there like the other wicked who have rest - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:47: And it says further afterward, that one who desecrates the Sabbath publicly is judged forever, even on the Sabbath itself, while the rest of the wicked who kept the Sabbath go out to see the judgment of those who did not keep the Sabbath; and of them it is said (Isaiah 66:24), "and they shall go forth and look upon the corpses of the men who rebelled against Me, for their worm shall not die, nor their fire be quenched, and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh." "For their worm shall not die" - from the body; "nor their fire be quenched" - from the soul. And they explained: what is "abhorrence" [dera'on]? "Enough seeing" [dai re'iyah] - for all the wicked say, "enough of this sight!"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:48: And in the Tikkunim (page 49b) it is explained there that there is a Gehinnom for the nefesh, ruach, and neshamah [the three levels of soul], which are called "the candle of the LORD, the soul (neshamah) of man" - and it says that ner [candle] is [an acronym for] nefesh, ruach, neshamah; and it says, whoever guards "the candle of the LORD, the soul of man" through Torah, through the positive and negative commandments, the fire of Gehinnom does not rule over him - and this corresponds to the liver, the gall, and the spleen: the liver is red fire, the gall is green fire, the spleen is black fire, and the diaphragm/lobe is the sum of them all, a dark techelet [sky-blue] - to this point. And so it further says there: gall, liver, and spleen are the exile for the neshamah, ruach, and nefesh - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:49: And I have seen fit to copy for you here the seven impure Heichalot [Chambers] that Rabbi Shimon brought in Parashat Pekudei, which my teacher, peace be upon him, copied in the book Pardes in the Holy Tongue; therefore I will copy his own words:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:50: In the first Heichal, called Bor [Pit] - and the pit is empty, and whoever comes to enter it has no support to hold onto so as not to fall, but rather all things push him to fall into it. In this Heichal there is one appointed officer named Dumah, and he stands here in this Heichal, and he stands at the entrance of the first Heichal of holiness from the outside, with several angels of destruction, to seize the souls that the holy angel Bohari'el pushes away, as I explained in the Gate of the Holy Heichalot, chapter 1.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:51: Under this officer Dumah there is another officer, named Patut, and under his hand are several thousands and myriads of angels of destruction; and he is appointed to entice people from the good way, to gaze upon adultery and lewdness - as his name, so is his deed. And all the angels of destruction who are with him go before people so that their eyes be drawn to transgression, and this officer is also called Sarsarim [brokers/pimps], for he is the broker of transgression. And this officer stands at the grave at the time the body is judged, and he pokes out his eyes, because he was led astray by his counsel - for such is the way of the husk [kelipah]: to accuse below and ascend, to prosecute above and descend, and take his soul; and whoever is drawn after him, he himself takes vengeance from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:52: Within this Heichal are several snakes and scorpions that bite the soul as it enters there. Over this whole Heichal is one appointed officer, named Gimguma, and he is red like a rose; and he stands to accuse when a person's prayer is rejected from the first Heichal of holiness, as I explained in the Gate of the Heichalot, chapter 1; and when this one receives that rejected prayer, it ascends with it up to the seventh Heichal of the husk, and from there it teaches guilt about him and recalls his sins - and this is what the verse says (Job 1:6), "and Satan also [gam] came" - "gam" is the name of Satan, who is Gimguma.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:53: And under his hand are several angels of destruction appointed to seize every vile word or every blemished word that a person utters with his lips, and they guard it; and when a person then utters from his mouth words of holiness, such as words of Torah or prayer, then those holy words are defiled with that impurity he uttered from his mouth beforehand, and then, as it were, the power of holiness is weakened - and then woe to him, woe to the soul of that sinner.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:54: Further, in this Heichal, over all these officers, there is one appointed officer named Tafsurinya, and under his hand several angels of destruction; and they are appointed over all those things a person casts away from his hand in anger, and they take that thing and bring it up above, and say, this is the offering of so-and-so, brought near to us; and they proclaim and say, woe to so-and-so, who went astray after a foreign god - and a heavenly voice goes out a second time and says, woe to them, for they have strayed from Me. And this Heichal is called "Satan of the Pit."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:55: The second Heichal is called Shachat, and it is impure and it is dark. In this Heichal there are three gates to three sides. At the first gate stands one appointed officer named Ashtariah, and under his hand several thousands and myriads of officers; and they are appointed over those who emit seed in vain, who do not see the face of the Shechinah - and these come and defile him in this world, and afterward, when his soul departs, these seize and bring him in to be judged by them; and these are called "boiling emission of seed," and they take the heat of the transgression and the seed and bring it up above, and this causes the holy covenant to be subjugated under the husks.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:56: At the second gate there is one appointed officer named Taskifa, and he is appointed over all those who consort with animals or with the severe forbidden relations of the Torah, and under his hand several thousands and myriads of angels of destruction, and their way with this person is like the way of those we mentioned above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:57: In this Heichal there is one appointed officer named "the Cup of Poison," and all those executed by the court who drank the cup of poison in this world are saved from the cup of poison of the World to Come. And what is the cup of poison? When the soul leaves the body, this officer, called the Cup of Poison, seizes him and gives him to drink the cup of poison, and in this cup are three drops: one is gravel, one is bitter as death, and one is fixing/setting. In this Heichal stands one appointed officer named Atzi Ariel, and from there they give him drink on the day of death - and this is the "three drops of the sword of the Angel of Death" that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, spoke of.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:58: At the third gate there is one appointed officer named Sangadiel, and he is appointed over all those who bring in and defile their covenant with a foreign woman's daughter, and all those who defile themselves with a gentile woman. Here the images of the women with whom they defiled themselves through this officer, and through the thousands of officers under his hand, are formed; and when his soul departs, they defile it in that image, and it is bound with him in the Heichal. And this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 3b), on "and he did not heed her, to lie beside her, to be with her" (Genesis 39:10) - "to lie beside her" in this world; "to be with her" - bound with her in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:59: Within this Heichal is one impure spirit, and upon it hang all sorceries and all kinds of divinations, and all of them hang upon the impurity of boiling seed; and this was the wisdom of Balaam the wicked, who would defile himself with his donkey, and then his sorceries would succeed. And for this reason this Heichal is called "impure Shachat" - for "impure it is; impure shall it be called."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:60: Under this upper spirit, there is in this Heichal yet another impure spirit named Sartiah, and several thousands and myriads of angels of destruction are under him; and they are ready at the time a dream descends from the side of holiness - this spirit and all the angels of destruction with him descend with that dream and mix with it, and inform that person of foolish words mixed with the true dream. And so [it accords with] the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory: just as it is impossible to have grain without straw, so it is impossible to have a dream without vain matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:61: And from the side of this Heichal go forth two spirits, who transform themselves sometimes into men and sometimes into women; and when the upper impure spirits travel, from the side of their travel two flames and blazes come into being, and go and spread through the world and appear to people in a dream in the form of beautiful women, and defile them with a seminal emission; and all this comes to one who is drawn after their words, and draws their spirit upon himself through his deeds. And this is what the Torah said (Deuteronomy 23:10), "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing" - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained: that one should not have improper thoughts by day, lest he come to impurity by night, Heaven forfend.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:62: And concerning this matter, they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (130a), in these words: one officer stands for this secret, over that female of the north, among all those bands of impurity - Sanugiria is his name; and at the time that smoke bends its path and ascends, this officer and sixty thousand myriads of other camps all present themselves to receive it and be nourished from it, and they stand in that female, and enter through one gate called Keri [nocturnal emission]. And this is the secret of what is written (Leviticus 26:21), "and if you walk contrary [keri] with Me, then I will also walk contrary [keri] with you," and so on, "in the fury of keri" - in that anger that emerges from the gate of keri; and these are the ones that roam about at night. And at the time souls go out to ascend, to appear above, these go out and accuse them so that they cannot ascend, except for those holy pious ones who cleave the firmaments and the airs and ascend. And these bands of impurity go out and tell people false things and appear to them in other images and laugh at them until they emit seed, and they are called "the masters of keri," because they go out through the gate of keri that they themselves cause. And at the time the fat portions and limbs [of sacrifices] are consumed, that smoke intoxicates them and nourishes them according to their honor - so is their sustenance, whatever is fitting for them; and through this they do not go out and do not roam in the Holy Land - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:63: And what it said, "that smoke bends" - it explained this above the passage, and we have not written it; and its explanation is that in the daily morning offering and the daily afternoon offering, the wind did not overcome the pillar of smoke, but at night the smoke would of itself bend toward the north side, so that these masters of keri would be nourished from it, so that they would not roam in the Land of Israel. And concerning the matter of one who has a seminal emission, it is further explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (19b, 55a); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:64: The third Heichal is called Heichal Ofel [Chamber of Gloom], and it is darker and gloomier than the previous ones, and it is called Dumah - for although we said that he [Dumah] descends to the first Heichal, his main seat is in this Heichal; and corresponding to it, the evil inclination is called Sonei [Enemy/Hater].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:65: In this Heichal there are four gates, and over them four appointed officers, as we shall explain. At the first gate there is one appointed officer named Katratia, and he stands with the power of wrath when judgment is stretched taut over the world, and it is the stumbling of the wicked; of this it is said (Proverbs 4:19), "the way of the wicked is like darkness; they know not at what they stumble." This officer stands at the crossroads to trip up, with his plague, those who walk alone on the roads and in the marketplaces, and he can harm them if he encounters them - and this is when he rules in the world through the strength of judgment stretched taut, Heaven forfend.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:66: At the second gate there is one appointed officer named Sangadiel (variant: Hangeriel), and under his hand several thousands and myriads of angels of destruction, and they all stand to receive the notes of judgment from outside the third Heichal, the Heichal of holiness. And when he receives the notes of judgment, he descends to the two previous Heichalot, Shachat and Bor, and there he has several thousands and myriads of angels of destruction, and they all roam the world to complete that judgment, Heaven forfend.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:67: At the third gate there is one appointed officer named Angiriyahun, and he is appointed over all the fevers that burn within the bones, and all kinds of evil illnesses that burn and consume the body, and from him go forth several thousands and myriads of officers appointed over this matter like him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:68: At the fourth gate there is one appointed officer named Askarah [Croup], and he is appointed over the killing and death of infants up to the age of thirteen years, and he appears as a woman who raises and nurses them and plays with them and [then] strangles them, and their soul is handed over to the angel Azriel, who is in the third Heichal of holiness, as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:69: In the middle of this Heichal stands one spirit called Agirisyon, and he is appointed over the death of young men from the age of thirteen to twenty, of whom it is said (Proverbs 13:23), "and there is that is swept away without justice" - for since they are not guarded when they are young, because of their poor discipline, and he sees a sign in them that they will sin and become corrupt, he kills them before they come to sin; and of this it is said (Genesis 1:31), "and behold, it was very good" - this is the Angel of Death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:70: From this Heichal spread out two spirits named Af and Cheimah [Anger and Wrath], and these Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, saw when he descended from the mountain, and said (Deuteronomy 9:19), "for I was afraid of the anger [af] and the wrath [cheimah]"; and under their hand are several thousands and myriads of angels of destruction, and they are all appointed over all those who hear a ban or excommunication from the mouth of a Torah authority and do not take it to heart, and likewise over all those who mock words of Torah or the sages; and so they all count and go to provoke all those who occupy themselves with Torah, and likewise in the performance of a commandment, so that they will not rejoice in it and will grieve over it instead.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:71: Under these spirits there is one spirit named Sichsicha, and when a person informs on his fellow or stirs up strife against him, this one is aroused together with that informing, to complete the matter and to kill through that informing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:72: Come and see: although the Holy One, blessed be He, has set for all beasts and snakes a time for shedding their skin, nevertheless all of it depends on evil speech and informing. When a person informs against his fellow, the lower beasts shed their skin and give forth cries, and those cries ascend above to the Heichal called Bor, where there are many snakes and many scorpions, as I explained above, and they all teach provocation to arouse the primordial serpent, the great serpent, and he sheds his skin, and all his bow-companies - meaning his camps and his forces - separate from him and he brings them down below into the Heichalot, and he ascends to speak provocation through that informing; and were it not for the shedding of his skin, no one could stand before him - may the Merciful One save us! And all this is because of the strength of informing and evil speech, and it is not for nothing that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said that it is a graver transgression than sexual immorality, idolatry, and bloodshed.
